A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SiM3D benchmark. All pages, including the supplementary material, are readable; text, equations, tables, and figures can be matched across additions, relocations, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection and segmentation experiments with adapted ADS baselines in Tables 3–5, alongside dataset analyses and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds AST evaluations, single-view and grayscale controls, and synthetic-to-real and anomaly-type analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed multiview adaptation remains unchanged: project per-view anomaly maps into voxels, aggregate by maximum pooling, and take the volume maximum for detection. Existing baseline adaptations are retained; AST expands the comparison methods without revising this procedure.

E1.justification: Section S.8 adds evaluation on grayscale MVTec AD and a single-view SiM3D test scenario. The eight-class SiM3D dataset and its real2real and synth2real coverage remain unchanged. The anomaly-type analysis subdivides existing defects.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 add AST with RGB and RGB+Depth inputs while retaining all previous quantitative comparators. Figures 5 and D replace BTF with AST in the corresponding qualitative comparisons; BTF remains represented in the new multimodal Figure E.

E3.justification: Existing SiM3D splits, preprocessing, input resolution, and V-AUPRO@1% evaluation are unchanged. New analyses introduce single-view testing, grayscale MVTec evaluation with 2D AUPRO@30%, train–test FID measurement, and separate evaluation of 2D versus combined 3D and multimodal defects.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's modality comparisons and qualitative examples, Sections S.7–S.9 test several central benchmark assumptions: synthetic-data quality versus transfer gaps, nominal-sample outliers, single-view versus multiview detection, grayscale effects, and performance by anomaly type. Tables C–D and Figure F provide substantial new diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new experiments continue reporting point estimates and class averages without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All retained numerical rows in Tables 3–5 are unchanged. Adding AST changes the best reported segmentation scores across Tables 4–5 from 0.671/0.620 to 0.699/0.695 for real2real/synth2real. AST RGB also reports synth2real detection of 0.544 versus PatchCore's 0.540. New controls, Tables C–D, and qualitative outputs substantially expand the findings.

T1.justification: The voxel-grid definitions and PRO/AUPRO mathematics are unchanged. The displayed PRO equation becomes inline mathematics, with equivalent content. The added empirical analyses introduce no new mathematical assumptions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and final discussion retain the same central contributions: a single-instance, multiview, multimodal 3D benchmark, real-to-real and synthetic-to-real setups, voxel-based evaluation, and adapted reference baselines. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 qualifies the previous image-only advantage with depth-native AST and emphasizes a larger transfer gap for detection than segmentation. New supplementary discussion attributes detection failures to nominal-score outliers, argues that grayscale does not explain benchmark difficulty, interprets anomaly-type differences, and explains limitations of comparing 2D and voxel segmentation.

D1.justification: v2 documents AST's EfficientNet-B5 features and 1540 × 1540 × 3 inputs, supplies its codebase attribution and MIT license, and replaces the general laboratory link with a SiM3D project link. Existing implementation details and the conditional future-release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: AST, already cited as reference 32 in v1, receives a dedicated explanation in Section 2 and more explicit positioning among multimodal approaches. The bibliography's membership and SiM3D's broader novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted revisions to the results discussion, removes numbered subheadings within Section 3, adds acknowledgments and three analytical supplementary sections, and renumbers retained appendix sections. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are preserved.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands with diagnostic Tables C–D, a comprehensive multimodal comparison in Figure E, and an outlier illustration in Figure F. Tables 3–5 gain AST rows, and Figures 5 and D replace BTF columns with AST. The earlier dataset-overview Figures E–G are retained as Figures G–I.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's largely aggregate evidence, v2 adds useful controls for the multiview and multimodal rationale and a depth-native baseline that refines the transfer-failure interpretation. These strengthen the benchmark's empirical support. The gain is limited by brief descriptions of the new controls and an inaccurate detection-winner statement: Section 5 still names PatchCore for synth2real, although Table 3 reports AST RGB at 0.544 versus 0.540.
